transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I don’t enjoy anything I used to love—church socials, baking, even talking with neighbors all feel empty now. It just feels like all the joy has been completely drained out of my life, and I don't know what to do.
How long have you been feeling this way, with everything feeling empty and joyless?

It’s been weighing on me steadily for about seven months now. It really started sinking in when the first holidays and church events came and went without my mother. Since then, this empty feeling just hasn't lifted.

You mentioned that this empty feeling started after the holidays and church events following your mother's passing; have you experienced any periods of improvement or significant worsening in your mood since then?

No, there haven't been any periods of relief or improvement at all. This heavy sadness has just been steady and constant for the past seven months. It feels like a continuous, heavy cloud weighing on me every single day without any break.

Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or energy levels since you started feeling this way, or have these aspects of your daily life remained relatively unchanged?

Yes, food has completely lost its taste and I often skip meals, so my clothes are fitting much looser now. I'm also constantly exhausted; even a simple shower feels like running a marathon, so I end up just sitting in my chair for hours because I have no energy.
Can you tell me more about your thoughts and feelings about your mother's passing, and do you often find yourself thinking about her or wishing you could have done something differently?

Her unexpected passing ten months ago has left me with an overwhelming guilt, and I've become convinced her death was actually a punishment from God directed at me. I even hear her voice scolding me in the hallway, saying I ruined everything and am just a burden now. It makes me feel like everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.
Can you describe more about these voices you hear, like your mother's, and how often you hear them, to help me understand what you're experiencing?

I hear my mother's voice clear as day scolding me in the hallway, mostly at night when the house gets really quiet. She says things like, "You ruined everything, Barbara," or "You’re a burden to everyone now." I know she is gone and that no one else hears it, but it still sounds so real to me.
Do you also see things that aren't there, like shadows or your mother's image, or is it just her voice that you hear?

No, I don't see any shadows or my mother's image at all. It is strictly just her voice that I hear scolding me in the hallway when the house gets quiet. I've never seen anything that isn't there, it's only the sound of her voice.
Do you believe the voice you hear, your mother's voice, is a real voice that others should be able to hear as well, or do you understand it as a product of your own mind?

I know she is gone and that no one else in the house can hear her, so I understand that others shouldn't be able to hear it. But when it happens, it sounds so clear and real to me that it's hard to explain. It just feels like it's happening right there in the hallway.
When you hear your mother's voice, do you think it's coming from inside your mind or from outside, like it's actually happening in the hallway?

It feels like it is coming from outside my head, clear as day right there in the hallway. Even though I logically know my mother is gone and others can't hear it, it sounds like she is actually standing there scolding me. She tells me so clearly that I ruined everything and that I'm just a burden to everyone now.
Do you ever think that these voices or the guilt you feel might be a part of your own thoughts or feelings, rather than an actual reflection of reality or your mother's true opinions?

Logically, I know she's gone and people tell me these things are just in my head, but in those quiet moments, the guilt feels absolutely true. Her voice sounds so incredibly real that I can't help but believe what she's saying about me. It just feels like I really did ruin everything, even if I try to tell myself otherwise.

When you hear your mother's voice, even though you know it's not real to others, do you think it's possible that your mind is playing a trick on you, or do you still believe it's actually your mother trying to communicate with you?

Intellectually, I know my mother is gone and no one else can hear her, so it must be my mind playing tricks on me. But in the quiet of the night, the voice sounds so incredibly real and hurtful. It just makes me feel like such a burden to everyone.

When you're hearing your mother's voice and feeling this overwhelming guilt, do you ever feel like you're losing touch with what's real and what's not, or do you always have a sense that these experiences, although very real-feeling, are not actually happening in the external world?

While I logically know my mother is gone and others can't hear her voice, it still feels incredibly real to me. But beyond that, I am deeply convinced that the signs from God, like the church bells ringing off-time and the flickering streetlight outside, are real messages meant just for me. Even though people try to tell me it's all in my head, I truly believe those signs are real.
Can you tell me more about these signs from God you mentioned, like the church bells and the flickering streetlight, and how they relate to your feelings of guilt and your mother's voice?

When the church bells ring off-time or the streetlight outside my window flickers, it feels like direct signs from God punishing me for my mom's death. Those signs, along with hearing her voice call me a burden, just reinforce this deep guilt and make me believe that everyone would be better off if I disappeared. I know others say it's not real, but to me, it feels so painfully and undeniably true.
Do you think these signs from God and your mother's voice are related to your own feelings of guilt and sadness, or do you believe they are objective messages from an external source?

To me, these signs and her voice feel incredibly real, especially the belief that God is punishing me because of my intense guilt over my mother's death. However, I also recognize that they only started after I fell into this deep sadness, so it feels like a painful mix of my own overwhelming grief and what feel like real messages.

When you experience these signs from God and hear your mother's voice, do you feel like you're in control of your thoughts and actions, or do you feel like something or someone else is controlling them?

I don't feel like anyone else is controlling my thoughts or actions. I still feel like I am the one making my own choices, even though the sadness and guilt make it very hard to do much of anything at all.
I'm sorry, doctor, but I didn't quite understand what you just said. It sounded a bit garbled and cut off. Could you please repeat your question for me?

Do you think that the voices you hear and the signs from God are a result of your own grief and sadness, or do you believe they are separate from your feelings and are actually real messages or events?

I know these experiences only started after I sank into this deep sadness, but they feel completely real to me. I am truly convinced those signs from God are real messages punishing me, no matter how much people tell me it's in my head. And even though I know my mother is gone and others can't hear her, her voice sounds clear as day and feels so real.

Do you think it's possible that your feelings of guilt and sadness are contributing to these experiences, such as hearing your mother's voice and seeing signs from God, or do you believe they are entirely separate and real?

I know these experiences only started after I fell into this deep sadness and guilt over losing my mother. But even though I intellectually know she is gone and others tell me these signs aren't real, in the moment they feel so completely real and convincing that it is hard to separate them from my grief.
Do you think there was a period when your sadness and guilt were at their worst before these voices and signs from God started, or did they all begin around the same time?

The deep sadness and losing interest in everything definitely came first. I had already been feeling completely empty and hopeless for quite a while before I ever started hearing my mother's voice or seeing those signs. They only began after I had already sunk into this deep depression.

When you hear your mother's voice or see the signs from God, do you think they are a direct result of your sadness and guilt, or do you believe they are separate entities that are happening to you regardless of your emotional state?

I believe they are deeply tied to my sadness and guilt, especially since these experiences only started after I fell into this deep depression. When they are happening, they feel incredibly real—like God is truly punishing me and my mother is actually calling me a burden. But I know I never had these painful thoughts or heard her voice before I became so overwhelmed by grief.
Have you ever had a period where the voices or signs from God stopped or significantly decreased, even if only for a short time, since they first started?

No, they haven't stopped or decreased at all since they first started. Ever since I fell into this deep depression, these voices and signs have been constant, happening almost every night without any real break or relief.
Have you ever had any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, or have you only experienced hearing your mother's voice and seeing signs from God?

No, I have never seen things that aren't actually there. My experiences are really just hearing my mother's voice scolding me in the dark, and interpreting real things—like the church bells or the flickering streetlight—as signs from God.

Do you think that if you were to receive treatment for your depression, these voices and signs from God might lessen or go away, or do you believe they would continue regardless of how your depression is treated?

Since the voices and signs only started after I fell into this deep sadness, I suppose they might be linked, so treating the depression could help. But honestly, this heavy gray cloud feels so permanent right now that I have a hard time believing anything will ever make them go away.

Do you think the voices and signs from God would still be present if your sadness and depression were to significantly improve, or do you believe they are inextricably linked to your current emotional state?

I believe they are directly tied to how terrible I feel right now. I never heard my mother's voice or saw those signs from God before I fell into this deep, heavy sadness, so I think they only happen because of this depression.
Do you think that if your depression were treated and you started feeling better, the voices and signs from God would still be there, or would they fade away as your mood improves?

I think they would probably go away if I could finally lift this heavy depression and feel like myself again. These voices and signs only started after I fell into this deep, heavy sadness, and I never experienced anything like this back when I was happy and active before my mother passed.

Do you think the voices and signs from God would still be present if your sadness and depression were to significantly improve, or do you believe they are inextricably linked to your current emotional state?

I believe they are completely tied to how low I feel right now. I never had these thoughts about God punishing me or heard my mother's voice back when I was feeling okay and still enjoying my life. They only started after I sank into this deep sadness and lost interest in everything, so they must be linked to how depressed I am.

Do you think the voices and signs from God would still be present if your sadness and depression were to significantly improve, or do you believe they are inextricably linked to your current emotional state?

I really believe they are completely tied to how empty and down I feel. I never heard my mother's voice or saw those signs from God before I fell into this deep, heavy sadness after she died. It feels like they only happen because I am feeling so low and empty right now.
Do you think that the voices you hear and the signs from God would still be present if you were no longer feeling depressed and had regained interest in the things you used to enjoy?

No, I don't think they would still be there if I wasn't depressed. I never heard my mother's voice or saw those signs before I fell into this deep sadness and lost interest in my life; they only started after the depression took over.
Do you think that the voices and signs from God would still be present if your sadness and depression were to completely go away and you were back to your normal self?

I don't think they would be present at all. Back when I was feeling like my normal self and enjoying my life, I never experienced anything like this. Since they only started after I fell into this deep depression, I believe they would completely disappear if the sadness went away.

Do you think the voices you hear and the signs from God are a direct result of your feelings of guilt and sadness, or do you believe they are separate entities that would continue even if your mood were to improve?

I believe they are a direct result of my sadness and guilt. They only started after I fell into this deep depression after my mother died, and I never experienced anything like this back when I was happy and active. I think they would go away if my mood improved.

The presence of auditory hallucinations, specifically hearing her mother's voice, and delusional thoughts, such as believing she is a burden and that God is punishing her, support this diagnosis.
